nahhas-irab:1-5.t:
فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً (5)
وَالْعادِياتِ is genitive by the wāw of oath. The scholars have two views on its meaning. Mujāhid and ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is the horses; and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is the camels, and Ibn Masʿūd said the same. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: A man asked me about وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحاً (1), and I said: it is the horses. He went to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and informed him, and he sent for me and had me brought, and said to me: "Do you speak about the Book of Allah without knowledge? By Allah, the first expedition was Badr, and we had only two horses with us: a horse of al-Zubayr and a horse of al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad. The runners (al-ʿādiyāt) are only from ʿArafa to al-Muzdalifa, and from al-Muzdalifa to Minā."
A parallel to this is what al-Buhlūl ibn Isḥāq ibn al-Buhlūl ibn Ḥassān narrated to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways narrated to us: Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī narrated to us, saying: I was with Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, and a man came to him and said: "O Abū Ḥamza, I am a man who has never performed the pilgrimage (ṣarūra); I have never made the Ḥajj, so teach me some of what Allah, Glorified, has taught you." He said: "Do you read the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then begin, and read بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ, five verses: وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحاً (1) فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً (2) فَالْمُغِيراتِ صُبْحاً (3) فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً (4) فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً (5). Do you know what this is?" He said: "No." He said: "«والعاديات ضبحا» is the departure from ʿArafa; فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً (2) is to al-Muzdalifa; فَالْمُغِيراتِ صُبْحاً (3): they do not press on until morning; فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً (4) فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً (5) is the day of Minā."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The scholars disagreed on the meaning of فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً. The position of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Ibn Masʿūd is that it is the camels. Mujāhid and ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: (it is) people kindling fire so that others may see it. Others narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: the horses. Qatāda said: the horses kindle war. ʿIkrima said: al-mūriyāt are the tongues. Abū Jaʿfar said: There is no evidence indicating that any of these views should be specified, so the correct thing is to say that it applies to everyone who kindles, given that the meaning is one, the implied form being "by the Lord of the runners".
ضَبْحاً was put in the accusative because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). From Ibn ʿAbbās: al-ḍabḥ is their blowing through their lips. قَدْحاً was put in the accusative as a maṣdar, because the meaning of «فالموريات» is "those that strike sparks (al-qādiḥāt)". «فالمغيرات»: from Ibn ʿAbbās, that it is the horses, and from Ibn Masʿūd, that it is the camels. «ضبحا» [Translator's note: so in the text; evidently صُبْحاً is meant] is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً (4): al-Farrāʾ said: the hāʾ is a pronoun for the valley, which has not been mentioned before, because the meaning is known. Abū al-Jawzāʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: al-naqʿ is the dust. Wasaṭna, wassaṭna and tawassaṭna are one (in meaning).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: He says: (حُصِّلَ means) brought out into the open.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: «إنّ» took kasra because of the lām. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that it is permissible to give it fatḥa together with the lām, because it (the lām) is redundant (zāʾida): its entering is like its leaving, except that it conveys emphasis.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: The exegetes hold that its meaning is "ungrateful", i.e., ungrateful for His favours. Al-Ḥasan said: he is resentful toward his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and blames Him for the afflictions that befall him, and forgets the favours.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَإِنَّهُ, i.e., and his Lord, عَلى ذلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: وَإِنَّهُ, i.e., and man, لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ: there are several views on its meaning. It has been said: (he is) of intense strength. The view of al-Farrāʾ is that the meaning is that man is intense in love of good; so the implied form according to him is "he, in love of good, is intense in love", then what came after شديد was omitted. The third view — I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: (it is) as you say "I honour so-and-so for you", i.e., for your sake; i.e., and he, for the sake of love of good, i.e., wealth, is "intense", i.e., miserly.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: It is not permissible for «يعلم» to govern «إذا», nor «لخبير»; rather the operator in it according to Muḥammad ibn Yazīd is «بعثر». And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās. [Translator's note: the entry breaks off here; the report continues in the next entry.]
